title: Normalize invoice line allocations for burst credits and duplicate usage records
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Summary:
We are seeing customer invoices where burst quota credits and mid-cycle quota bumps are not being applied consistently across Stripe invoice lines and the NetSuite export. Two root symptoms were observed: (1) duplicated hourly usage events (same usage_uuid emitted twice from the collector) are causing double-counted invoice lines after aggregation, and (2) credits or quota-bumps that become effective partway through an hourly window are applied at coarse granularity, which misaligns Stripe line merging and NetSuite GL allocation IDs. This ticket implements a reconciliation fix that applies offsets deterministically at the usage-event granularity, de-duplicates by usage_uuid, and updates the export mapping so NetSuite line items match Stripe invoice lines for downstream accounting and auditability.
acceptance_criteria: Duplicate usage events are deduplicated using usage_uuid; tests cover duplicate, out-of-order, and partial-duplicate cases
Credits and quota-bump offsets are applied at usage-event granularity—Stripe invoice lines must match the NetSuite export allocation_id for affected customers in test exports
Reconciliation job is idempotent: re-running the export for an invoice should not create new invoice lines or change totals
Existing invoice-level totals (for a representative sample of 50 customers across plans) do not regress beyond +/- 0.5% after fix; any changes are explainable and documented
Integration tests with sandbox Stripe and NetSuite demonstrate canonical mapping and include a rollout checklist for production cutover
steps: Add deduplication stage in hourly-usage-aggregator: filter by usage_uuid with TTL-based seen-set to handle late arrivals
Change offset application to attach credit_effective_time to each usage_event and compute adjusted_charge at event level
Update Stripe line creation so lines are grouped by (customer_id, product_id, allocation_id) after event-level adjustments rather than by hour bucket
Modify NetSuite export transformer to consume event-level allocation_id and emit a 1:1 mapping to Stripe line_id (store stripe_line_foreign_id in export row)
Add migration step to backfill mapping for open invoices in last 30 days and reconcile with finance team
implementation_notes: Performance: The dedupe seen-set will use redis with an expiry equal to max_allowed_lateness + 1 hour; estimated extra memory ~300MB for peak traffic
Ordering: reconciliation must sort by (usage_event_time, credit_effective_time) to ensure deterministic offset application for boundary events
Idempotency: include reconciliation_job_id and source_batchId in NetSuite export rows to avoid duplicate posts
Fallback: if NetSuite export mapping fails for a batch, emit a rollback manifest and pause automated invoice finalization for affected customers
Compatibility: Keep legacy hourly-aggregate export mode behind a feature flag (billing.event_level_offsets) for 2 weeks of A/B validation
test_plan: Unit tests: dedupe logic, event-level offset math, grouping changes
Integration tests: end-to-end against stripe-sandbox + netsuite-sandbox using a generator that creates burst credits mid-hour and duplicate usage events
Load test: validate aggregator latency stays under existing SLO (p95 < 600ms extra) with Redis dedupe enabled
Regression: compare totals for nightly billing snapshot before/after fix for a seeded set of customers
Finance sign-off: run pre-production export and verify GL mapping with accounting team
rollout_plan: Merge behind feature flag and deploy to staging
Run synthetic batch in staging and validate stripe-sandbox invoices + netsuite-sandbox rows
Enable feature for 10% of customers with low variance plans for 48h, monitor invoice diffs and alerts
Gradually increase to 50% and then 100% over 5 business days if no regressions
Run backfill for 30-day window once at >95% rollout and then coordinate with finance to mark invoices reconciled
